sentence_stem: Having been warned about the storm,
correct_completion: the sailors returned to the harbour early.
full_sentence: Having been warned about the storm, the sailors returned to the harbour early.
acceptable_variants: the crew headed back to port early.
the sailors turned back before dark.

options.text: the sailors ignored the weather report.
options.why_wrong: This is grammatically possible but contradicts the logic of the stem: the participle clause says the sailors were warned, so they would be expected to respond to the warning.

options.text: they having returned to the harbour early.
options.why_wrong: A perfect participle cannot serve as the main verb after a comma. The main clause needs a finite verb.

options.text: to return to the harbour early.
options.why_wrong: An infinitive cannot serve as the main verb of the sentence. The main clause needs a finite verb.

options.text: the sailors returned to the harbour early.

grammar_focus: Perfect passive participle clause ('having been' + past participle) with a shared subject
explanation: The perfect passive participle 'having been warned' introduces a clause whose subject is the sailors, so the main clause must continue with that same subject and a finite active verb.
translation: Ostrzeżeni o burzy, żeglarze wrócili wcześnie do portu.
